authorization: The owner asked for a refresh icon when an update is live ("full send"), then for the worthwhile follow-ups, then chose "Release and verify" when asked whether to release #575 and #576.

release.summary: An open page now learns when a newer deployment is live. GET /api/version answers the server's deployment ID (no-store). The page compares it with the ID Next.js builds into its client code (process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID), on tab focus or visibility and every 10 minutes, at most once a minute. When they differ, a small refresh icon with a dot shows beside the Visibible name in the reader and beside "Back to reading" on the other pages, with a polite status for screen readers. Tapping it reloads; nothing reloads on its own. #576 only corrects a comment: Next.js, not React, removes <html data-dpl-id>.
release.leftOut: Nothing else was waiting: production was main e5fa72ca (#571); main since then held only its release record (#572).

steps.convex: Not pushed: no convex/ change since production e5fa72ca.

steps.from: a clean detached checkout of origin/main with no .env.local, in .claude/worktrees/update-notice

smoke.after: GET https://visibible.com/api/version → 200, Cache-Control no-store, {"version":"dpl_34oyY3JzvX8FMRp51sDFPoJ7Vvu4"}, the same ID as the served pages' data-dpl-id. Four of John 3:16's client chunks contain that ID as a string literal, so the page's own version is built in. In the browser on visibible.com/john/3/16 a focus event made one /api/version request (200), no icon showed (same version), the status region was mounted empty, and the reader loaded normally. /about 200. The first release with the icon cannot announce itself: tabs opened before it run code without the icon, so the first live notice comes with the next release.
smoke.beforeRelease: npm test 1730/1730, tsc, lint (0 errors, 14 warnings as before), CI quality-gates on both PRs. Two production builds (dpl_versionA, dpl_versionB) behind a switching local proxy showed the icon after the switch and reloaded into B. Sol (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh) ran 3 rounds; its findings were fixed (the last after its budget). A two-axis code review and CodeRabbit ran; their findings were fixed.
